sentences.text: Shri M.P.S. Raghuwanshi, Sr. Advocate with Shri R.K. Shri  Advocate appeared for the petitioner.
Shri Shiv Pratap Singh Kushwah, - Advocate for the respon Shri Samar Ghuraiya - PP appearing on behalf of State.
Heard on I.A. No.6251/2025, first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

This appeal assails the judgment dated 27.08.2024 passed by the Second Additional Sessions Judge,
Sevada, District Datia in SC No.30/2019 whereby, appellant has been convicted under Section 363,
366, 376 of IPC with maximum of 10 years RI with fine and default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the matter.

entities.text:
Second Additional Sessions Judge,
Sevada, District Datia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned trial Court has erred in convicting the appellant and awarding jail sentence without appreciating the evidence in right perspective.
Appellant has already suffered near about 2 years and 2 months' of incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix is major and the proofs of age have been manipulated.

It has also been submitted that it is a matter of consent and the prosecutrix on her own violation had eloped with the appellant and married him in the temple at Mathura and lived with him for nearabout 1.5 months.
There are material contradictions and omissions in 2 CRA-11303-2024 the statements of witnesses.
The appellant was on bail during trial, however, he did not misuse the liberty so granted.
Final hearing of the appeal is likely to take some time.
The appellant shall abide by all the conditions as may be imposed by the Court.
Hence, prayed to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the application and submitted that the prosecutrix is minor girl and the appellant was aged about 32 years at the time of incident, thus,
consent cannot be considered.
DNA also found to be positive.
Hence he prayed for rejection of the application.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, especially looking to the allegations against the appellant, nature of Shashikant Tyagi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187939696/
1 offence, age of prosecutrix and her statement, this Court is not inclined to grant benefit of suspension of sentence to the appellant at this stage.

entities.text: Shashikant Tyagi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the application is dismissed.
